variants.name: Tagged envelope + dispatch table (portable baseline)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic C++ realization: a small POD header carrying a type tag, plus a dispatch table from tag to parse function. Nothing in the standard library supplies the metadata channel, so the token-to-parser registry is hand-written - a std::map<std::uint16_t, parser> or a switch on an enum. Prefer an enum tag over a string when the vocabulary is closed, and validate the tag before constructing any body type.
pitfalls: Reinterpreting a buffer as a struct is undefined behaviour when alignment or padding differ; read fields individually or use an explicitly packed representation.
A std::string token leaves the vocabulary open and makes every consumer pay a hash lookup and comparison; close the set with an enum where you can.
Registries keyed by RTTI (type_info/type_index) reintroduce the same class-name trust problem as Java default typing.

variants.name: FlatBuffers file identifier (buffer-level classification)
variants.implementation_notes: FlatBuffers is deliberately not self-describing, but a schema may declare a four-character file_identifier that lands at bytes 4-7 of every generated buffer, and generated code exposes a BufferHasIdentifier check. That yields a property-shaped classification decision before any table is opened; the token-to-parser registry maps the identifier to the right generated accessor. Choose it when buffers are also files or are archived and want a magic-number check; the FlatBuffers documentation itself recommends a union field instead for one of several messages sent over a network, which is the content-based sibling.
pitfalls: The identifier travels inside the payload, so a bridge that rewraps or compresses the buffer loses it; treat it as a file-format check, not as transport metadata.
It is only four characters and is optional per schema - buffers produced by calling Finish explicitly omit it, so the reader must handle its absence.

variants.name: gRPC metadata as the property channel
variants.implementation_notes: gRPC metadata is a real key-value header map carried over HTTP/2 headers and visible to interceptors before the request message is decoded. A custom key - keys must not start with grpc-, which is reserved - carries the type token, and a server interceptor resolves it against the registry so the deserialiser is chosen on the transport's own metadata channel. Choose it when one RPC method carries several logical message kinds or when a proxy that only reads headers does the routing.
pitfalls: The grpc- prefix is reserved for gRPC itself and servers limit request-header size (8 KiB suggested), so the token must stay tiny.
Binary metadata needs the -bin suffix and base64 framing; a plain token avoids that, but a mistyped key yields an empty lookup that must be treated as an error, not a default.
